# Solana wallet and transaction building for bots — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Solana wallet and transaction building for bots. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Definitions

- [statement] A null entry from getSignatureStatuses means the status was not found, not that the transaction failed. The method searches only a recent status cache unless searchTransactionHistory is true. A null can mean dropped, never landed, or evicted from the cache. Treat the transaction as dead only after block height passes lastValidBlockHeight and a history search also returns null. (medium confidence) — https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/guides/getsignaturestatuses.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction
- [statement] FullSend is a separate, access-gated Jito product: a Solana JSON-RPC sendTransaction endpoint that forwards signed transactions straight to current and upcoming leaders through stake-weighted QoS. It does not simulate transactions or track confirmation. Solana Compass reports that Jito's BAM maintenance notice says validators, FullSend users and standard bundle senders need take no action for the Alpenglow transition. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.jito.wtf/fullsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://solanacompass.com/news/jito-details-bams-alpenglow-plan-maintenance-mode-for-all-mainnet-nodes-no-firebam-during-the-transition
- [statement] FullSend is a separate, access-form-gated Jito service: a Solana-compatible JSON-RPC sendTransaction at https://mainnet.hudson.jito.wtf with an api_key query parameter, direct-to-leader SWQOS delivery, validator blacklists for MEV protection (default and custom, both on by default), and a browser-safe sendTransactionWeb that authenticates by authorized fee-payer signer. It runs no simulation and tracks no confirmation. Jito's BAM changelog says FullSend users needed no action during the Alpenglow BAM maintenance window. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://github.com/jito-labs/jito-docs/blob/main/docs/source/fullsend.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://bam.dev/blog/bam-changelog-sept-23-oct-9/
- [statement] A keypair file written by solana-keygen is a JSON array of exactly 64 byte values: the first 32 bytes are the Ed25519 secret seed and the last 32 bytes are the public key. Metaplex states the file 'must be a JSON array of 64 numbers'. (high confidence) — https://kevinheavey.github.io/solders/tutorials/keypairs.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-keypair/latest/source/src/lib.rs, https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets, https://mattmazur.com/2021/11/19/splitting-a-solana-keypair-into-a-public-and-private-keys/
- [statement] A Solana CLI keypair file is a JSON array of exactly 64 byte values: the first 32 are the Ed25519 secret seed and the last 32 are the public key. `solana-keygen new` writes it to ~/.config/solana/id.json unless --outfile is given (Agave builds home_dir/.config/solana/id.json). Metaplex states the file 'must be a JSON array of 64 numbers'. (high confidence) — https://kevinheavey.github.io/solders/tutorials/keypairs.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-keypair/latest/source/src/lib.rs, https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anza-xyz/agave/master/keygen/src/keygen.rs
- [statement] The base fee is a flat 5,000 lamports per required signature. It does not depend on the CUs the transaction requests or uses. The priority fee is charged on top of the base fee. (high confidence) — https://chorus.one/reports-research/transaction-latency-on-solana-do-swqos-priority-fees-and-jito-tips-make-your-transactions-land-faster · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/blog/solana-fees-in-theory-and-practice, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-transaction-v1
- [statement] @solana/kit is the renamed 2.x line of @solana/web3.js. It is functional (no classes except SolanaError), fully tree-shakable, uses Web Crypto Ed25519 so key and signing operations are async, supports native bigint, and has zero third-party dependencies. It is not backward-compatible with web3.js 1.x. (high confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/kit · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://blog.triton.one/intro-to-the-new-solana-kit-formerly-web3-js-2/, https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/tooling/web3js/migrate-to-v3
- [statement] Kit has no Connection or Transaction classes. Moving a web3.js v1 codebase to Kit means rewriting every call site, and libraries such as Anchor's TypeScript client did not plug into Kit. The @solana/compat package offers conversion helpers between legacy and Kit types. (high confidence) — https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/tooling/web3js/migrate-to-v3 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/kit
- [statement] A v0 message is a legacy message plus a 0x80 version prefix byte and an address_table_lookups array after the instructions. Each lookup names a table by its 32-byte address and lists one-byte writable and read-only indexes into it. The runtime appends the resolved writable addresses, then the read-only ones, to the static keys, and instructions index into that combined list. A lookup that selects no accounts fails sanitization. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/blob/master/message/src/versions/v0/mod.rs
- [statement] New table entries are not usable in the slot where they were added. The table stores last_extended_slot and last_extended_slot_start_index. While the current slot equals last_extended_slot, a lookup sees only the entries before that start index. A transaction that references a newer entry in the same slot fails. (high confidence) — https://docs.rs/solana-address-lookup-table-interface/3.1.0/src/solana_address_lookup_table_interface/state.rs.html · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs
- [statement] Do not catch -32015 and return null or 'not found'. It means the request failed on a versioned transaction, not that the transaction is missing. Helius says -32015 in logs already shows a project failing on versioned transactions. A payment-detection loop that swallows it reports a landed transaction as lost. (medium confidence) — https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/transaction-v1.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/core/transactions/versioned-transactions.mdx, https://dev.to/timothymycompc/solana-rpc-error-32015-why-4-in-10-transactions-vanish-from-your-app-26cm

## Structure and components

- [statement] A Solana keypair file is plaintext and the generation passphrase does not protect it. Anza's file-system wallet page says 'This file contains your unencrypted keypair', 'File system wallets are the least secure method of storing SOL tokens', and that even with a password 'that password applies to the recovery seed phrase, not the file'. Matt Mazur's walkthrough shows the CLI prompt itself saying the passphrase improves the seed phrase 'NOT the keypair file itself, which is stored as insecure plain text'. Anza's page gives no file-permission advice. (high confidence) — https://docs.anza.xyz/cli/wallets/file-system · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://mattmazur.com/2021/11/19/splitting-a-solana-keypair-into-a-public-and-private-keys/

## How it works

- [statement] A successful sendTransaction response returns only a signature. It does not show that the cluster will process or finalize the transaction. The caller must poll getSignatureStatuses, because the RPC can return a signature for a transaction that is later dropped. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-rpc-timeout-and-retries
- [statement] Fetching a blockhash at processed can pick a blockhash from a minority fork that the cluster later abandons. The transaction is then dropped with the blockhash not found. Official docs advise confirmed or finalized when polling getLatestBlockhash. Helius calls confirmed the best practice for sending and states that processed is not recommended for production-critical flows. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/blog/solana-commitment-levels, https://www.helius.dev/blog/how-to-deal-with-blockhash-errors-on-solana
- [statement] sendTransaction returns only the transaction id (the first signature). A successful response says nothing about whether the cluster will process or finalize the transaction, and the RPC can hand back a signature for a transaction that is later dropped. A bot must poll getSignatureStatuses to learn the outcome. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-rpc-timeout-and-retries, https://www.helius.dev/docs/rpc/guides/getsignaturestatuses.md
- [statement] A fee-bumped rebroadcast is a different transaction. Changing the compute-unit price changes the message, so the message hash and signature change and the AlreadyProcessed check does not link the two. RPC Fast describes rebroadcasting 'with a slightly higher priority fee' when a transaction is not processed within 2 slots. By the official guide's logic both versions can land while the blockhash is valid. Guard such intents on-chain (Circuit added a sequence-enforcer instruction with TTL checks) or accept duplicates. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.4.0/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx, https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-land-transactions-solana, https://circuittrading.notion.site/November-10-2024-JLP-Vaults-Post-Mortem-13b1385fd0f58031b7acde64235c4852
- [statement] Two intentionally identical transactions collide. The duplicate check keys on the whole message hash, so the same fee payer, instructions, accounts and blockhash give AlreadyProcessed on the second send. Change the message (a fresh blockhash or different instruction data) to send a distinct second transaction. Chainstack also warns that transactions can be treated as duplicates when many share a blockhash. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.4.0/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] Do not re-sign with a new blockhash while the first blockhash can still land. The Solana retry guide calls confirming expiry first 'very important' because both transactions can be accepted. Chainstack and the fardream library say the same. The safe order: rebroadcast identical bytes until block height is past lastValidBlockHeight, make a final status lookup, then rebuild. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error, https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction
- [statement] Jito tips and Solana priority fees are separate levers: the tip ranks the bundle in the Block Engine auction, the priority fee affects runtime scheduling. Tips do nothing when the leader is not Jito-Solana. For single transactions via Jito sendTransaction, Jito advises setting both a priority fee and a tip; Chainstack suggests a 70/30 split between them. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-mev-protection
- [statement] The Block Engine sendTransaction path (https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/transactions) proxies Solana's sendTransaction to the validator with MEV protection on by default and always sets skip_preflight=true, so the RPC does not simulate the transaction first. The query parameter bundleOnly=true sends the transaction only as a single-transaction bundle, which gives revert protection. When the send was made as a bundle, the bundle ID comes back in the x-bundle-id response header. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://gist.github.com/zhe-t/60938c69e29276b7a9f098e1b0672c79
- [statement] If transactions from your bundle show up on an explorer as individual failed transactions, suspect an uncled block. When a block built by a leader is not accepted by the supermajority, any party that received it can rebroadcast its transactions, and those go through the normal banking stage without bundle atomicity or revert protection. Jito's mitigations are pre- and post-account checks so a rebroadcast is harmless, minimizing leakage, and keeping the tip in the same transaction as the strategy. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use your own transaction signatures against your own RPC as the ground truth for 'landed'. Bundle-ID endpoints have short retention (five minutes in flight, recent slots for statuses) and DBI bundles are outside them; keep bundle-status polling for diagnosis only (in-flight state, drop reason). The jito-bundle crate likewise polls both the Jito API and Solana RPC. (medium confidence) — https://bam.dev/docs/bam/dbi/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/, https://docs.rs/crate/jito-bundle/0.1.4/source/FOR_USER.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Commitment guidance changed with Alpenglow. The Solana docs say to point new code at finalized, because it now arrives in about 150 ms, and to re-check every timeout, retry or UX delay tuned to 12.8-second finality. They say confirmed will be removed in a later release. Triton One warns not to move to finalized before the node runs Alpenglow, or requests wait the old 12.8 s. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/upgrades/alpenglow.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://blog.triton.one/alpenglow-and-your-triton-stack-what-to-update-before-mainnet/
- [statement] Maker Priority (MPP) and Preconfirmations are not general landing routes. MPP: enrolled market makers send pre-signed price updates to a separate UDP endpoint (PTPU) on each BAM Node; they are scheduled first in every auction batch, need no tip, but must pay at least 1 lamport per compute unit; Jito manages enrollment. Preconfirmations: a read-only stream of transactions a BAM leader has committed to executing, sold through Helius and Triton, with a p50 advantage of 5-10 ms over shred feeds in early tests; they are not finality and exist only for BAM leaders. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://github.com/jito-labs/jito-docs/blob/main/docs/source/mpp.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/jito-labs/jito-docs/blob/main/docs/source/preconfirmations.md, https://solanacompass.com/news/jito-bam-preconfirmations-go-live-on-solana-covering-34-of-network-stake, https://bam.dev/blog/bam-changelog-sept-23-oct-9/
- [statement] Triton extends getRecentPrioritizationFees with an optional percentile parameter, an integer from 1 to 10,000 (5000 is the median, steps of 0.01%). For each block it returns that percentile of the CU prices paid by non-vote transactions; with account addresses it takes the percentile over the transactions that write-lock each account and returns the highest. Without the parameter it returns the standard minimum. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.triton.one/solana/sending-transactions/priority-fees-api.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Resending identical signed bytes is harmless because the network executes at most one copy of a given signature. The duplicate risk comes only from building a second, different transaction. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx
- [statement] Once a blockhash has expired, resending the same signed bytes cannot succeed: the handler must fetch a fresh blockhash, re-sign and resend, and a generic HTTP retry wrapper does not do that. Retries consume blockhashes and can cost fees, and no retry strategy rescues a badly degraded network, so fail fast and alert. (medium confidence) — https://onfinality.io/en/learn/solana-rpc-timeout-and-retries · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] One web3.js user reported confirmTransaction throwing the block-height-exceeded error for a transaction that had already finalized, after sending with a confirmed blockhash and confirming at confirmed. The issue tracker bot closed it by pointing to the Agave repo, and no cause was recorded. Treat an expiry exception as a prompt to check the signature status before rebuilding. (low confidence) — https://github.com/solana-labs/solana/issues/35556
- [statement] Rebroadcasting identical signed bytes cannot execute twice. Agave's check_transactions rejects a message hash that is already in the StatusCache with AlreadyProcessed ('This transaction has already been processed'). The cost is an error, not a double spend. With preflight on, sendTransaction runs a simulation and returns any simulation error, so a Drift keeper-bot log shows 'Transaction simulation failed: This transaction has already been processed'. A rebroadcast loop must treat that error as 'look up the signature', not as failure. Re-sending with skipPreflight true, as the Solana guide's example does, avoids the error. (high confidence) — https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/6cd331bf6fd0e92c59e847a3aefaac16ff7b7eda/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/6cd331bf6fd0e92c59e847a3aefaac16ff7b7eda/rpc/src/rpc.rs, https://github.com/drift-labs/keeper-bots-v2/issues/130, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx
- [statement] A Jito bundle is a list of up to 5 fully signed transactions that execute sequentially, within a single slot, and atomically: if any transaction fails, none are committed. Bundles cannot cross slot boundaries. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.quicknode.com/builders-guide/tools/jito-bundles-by-jito-labs, https://cnitarot.github.io/papers/imc26_solana.pdf
- [statement] Transactions are submitted to the Block Engine (JSON-RPC POST /api/v1/bundles, method sendBundle, or gRPC) as base64 strings (recommended); base58 is slow and marked DEPRECATED in Jito's docs. Maximum 5 transactions per request. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/docs/sending-transactions/send-bundle
- [statement] Jito's default send rate limit is 1 request per second per IP per region, with no auth key needed for default sends; exceeding it returns a 429 or rate-limit error; higher limits need a ticket. Spreading sends across regional Block Engine endpoints (mainnet global plus Amsterdam, Dublin, Frankfurt and others) therefore multiplies capacity. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/
- [statement] A Jito bundle is a list of up to 5 fully signed transactions that the Block Engine passes to a Jito-Solana leader to execute sequentially and atomically within one slot. A bundle cannot cross a slot boundary, and if any transaction fails none of the transactions are committed. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://cnitarot.github.io/papers/imc26_solana.pdf, https://www.helius.dev/docs/sending-transactions/send-bundle
- [statement] The Block Engine runs parallel auctions. Bundles whose account-lock patterns intersect on a writable account ((w,w), (r,w) or (w,r)) compete in one auction; bundles that do not intersect, or that overlap only on reads, run in separate auctions. Within an auction bundles are ranked by requested tip per requested compute unit, and Jito submits the highest-paying combination to the validator up to a compute-unit limit. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/jito-explained-bundles-tips-mev-solana
_31 more problems, failure modes and limitations units in llms-full.txt#problems-failure-modes-and-limitations_

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] 'Transaction simulation failed: This transaction has already been processed' on a resend means an identical message is already in the status cache. Read the signature's status instead of treating the send as failed. A Drift keeper bot logged that error and then failed with a 30-second 'not confirmed' timeout; a Drift maintainer attributed this class of error to congestion or an RPC node that fell behind. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/drift-labs/keeper-bots-v2/issues/130 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.4.0/runtime/src/bank/check_transactions.rs
- [statement] Keypair files must stay out of git. Metaplex lists 'Never commit keypair files to git' and advises ignoring *.json. A CI secret scanner flags tracked files named id.json or *-keypair.json by filename alone, any JSON array of 64 integers 0-255, and base58 strings of about 86-90 characters. That scanner checks only the current tree, not history, so historical leaks need truffleHog or gitleaks, and exposed keys must be rotated rather than just deleted from git. (medium confidence) — https://metaplex.com/docs/solana/solana-keypairs-and-wallets · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://dev.to/sai_93caeceb4f6a4d9969910/a-free-github-action-that-fails-ci-on-leaked-solana-wallet-keys-how-i-built-and-shipped-3n9c
- [statement] A CU limit taken from a simulation can be too low at landing time, because account state changes between simulation and execution (swap routes through Token-2022 transfer hooks or changing tick arrays). The result is ComputationalBudgetExceeded and a paid, failed transaction. The sources suggest a 10-15% margin, re-simulating when a program is upgraded or the instruction mix changes, and caching typical CU use per transaction type instead of simulating every send. (medium confidence) — https://dev.to/verixia_233e4721792ce3390/optimizing-solana-compute-unit-limits-for-swap-execution-3di4 · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://orbitflare.com/blog/developers/solana-priority-fee-estimation, https://github.com/solana-labs/solana-web3.js/pull/2703
- [statement] Upgrading to web3.js v3 silently changes Connection's default commitment from finalized to confirmed. The code compiles unchanged, so the compiler cannot flag it; the official migration guide says 'omitted commitment now defaults to confirmed rather than finalized'. A bot that relied on finalized reads must pass the commitment explicitly on the Connection or per call, and should test against a real node because mocked tests keep passing with the old default. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-web3.js/blob/main/packages/web3.js/RELEASE_NOTES.md · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-web3.js/blob/main/docs/web3js-v1-to-v3-migration.md, https://www.quicknode.com/guides/solana-development/tooling/web3js/migrate-to-v3
- [statement] The table authority must sign every extend, freeze, deactivate and close. Entries are append-only, so an index always resolves to the same address (Anza made tables append-only to stop front-running). FreezeLookupTable sets the authority to None; after that the program refuses extend, deactivate and close ('Lookup table is frozen'), so the table's rent is locked for good. A bot that depends on someone else's table, such as a router's, must expect the authority to deactivate and close it, and should re-fetch table accounts before building instead of caching them indefinitely. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/solana-program/address-lookup-table/blob/main/program/src/processor.rs · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.anza.xyz/proposals/versioned-transactions

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A blockhash is valid for about 150 blocks. The sources quote this window as roughly 1 minute 19 seconds, 60-90 seconds, or 80-90 seconds, depending on slot time. A transaction not processed in that window must be rebuilt with a new blockhash. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.helius.dev/blog/how-to-deal-with-blockhash-errors-on-solana, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] Re-sign with a new blockhash only after the current block height exceeds lastValidBlockHeight. Before then, the original transaction may still land, and a re-signed copy with a different blockhash is a distinct transaction that can also execute. The user then sees the same action twice. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction, https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error
- [statement] Do not re-sign with a new blockhash until the original blockhash has expired. While it is still valid, both transactions can be accepted, and the user sees the same action twice. Re-sign only after the block height passes lastValidBlockHeight. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/solana-how-to-handle-the-transaction-expiry-error, https://github.com/fardream/confirm-solana-transaction
- [statement] Do not treat a processed status as done. The retry guide documents a transaction that a leader on a minority fork processed and that was dropped before it finalized, and the Solana docs say processed data can change if the cluster switches forks. Under Alpenglow processed is unchanged and means only that a bank executed the transaction. (high confidence) — https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/cookbook/transactions/retry.mdx · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/en/rpc/http/sendtransaction.mdx, https://github.com/solana-foundation/solana-com/blob/main/apps/media/content/upgrades/alpenglow.mdx
- [statement] The Block Engine's bundle result protocol separates outcomes: Accepted (forwarded to a validator, possibly several), and Rejected with one of StateAuctionBidRejected (bid too low for its state auction), WinningBatchBidRejected (won its state auction but lost against other winners), SimulationFailure (names the offending tx signature), InternalError, or DroppedBundle. Block engines simulate bundles and pick the most profitable combinations. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jito-labs/mev-protos/master/bundle.proto · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/
- [statement] Put the tip instruction in the same transaction as the strategy logic, with post-transaction checks, so a failed strategy does not pay the tip. If space is tight, put state assertions (slot, balance) in the tip transaction. A standalone tip transaction inside a bundle increases exposure to 'uncle bandit' rebroadcast of individual bundle transactions. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana
- [statement] Atomicity does not hold if a block is uncled: bundle transactions can be rebroadcast individually outside the bundle ('unbundling'). Jito says Jito itself never leaks bundles, but during uncled-block situations users are exposed. Mitigation is pre/post account checks inside the transactions so a lone rebroadcast tx is harmless. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana
- [statement] Tips only influence a leader that runs Jito-Solana. Jito warns that tips do not prioritize transactions at validators that are not Jito-Solana leaders, so tipping then is wasted. Bundle inclusion is therefore tied to the slots where a Jito-enabled validator produces blocks. (high confidence) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/ · keywords: Solana wallet and transaction building for bots · also: https://www.quicknode.com/builders-guide/tools/jito-bundles-by-jito-labs, https://rpcfast.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-jito-bundle-landing-rate-on-solana
